     7	/-!
     8	# The low-degree game
     9	
    10	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    11	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    12	the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
    13	invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    18	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    19	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    32	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    33	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    34	`def:ld-game` in
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    37	-/
    38	structure LdParams where
    39	  q : ℕ
    40	  m : ℕ
    41	  d : ℕ
    42	  k : ℕ
    43	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    44	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    45	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    46	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    47	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    48	
    49	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    50	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    51	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    53	-/
    54	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    55	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    56	
    57	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    58	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    59	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    61	-/
    62	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    63	
    64	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    65	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    66	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    67	-/
    68	inductive LdType where
    69	  | point
    70	  | aline
    71	  | dline
    72	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    73	
    74	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    75	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    77	-/
    78	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    79	
    80	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    81	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    83	-/
    84	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    85	
    86	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    88	-/
    89	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    90	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    91	
    92	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    93	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    94	-/
    95	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
    96	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
    97	
    98	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   100	-/
   101	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   102	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   103	
   104	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   105	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   106	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   107	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   108	-/
   109	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   110	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   111	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   112	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   113	
   114	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   115	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   116	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   117	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   119	-/
   120	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   121	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   122	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   123	
   124	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   125	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   126	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   127	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   128	-/
   129	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   130	  fun i => match i with
   131	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   132	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   133	  | .inr _ => 0
   134	
   135	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   136	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   137	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   138	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   139	-/
   140	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   141	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   142	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   143	  fun i => match i with
   144	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   145	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   146	  | .inr _ => 0
   147	
   148	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   149	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   150	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   151	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   153	-/
   154	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   155	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   156	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   157	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   158	  fun i => match i with
   159	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   160	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   161	  | .inr j => direction j
   162	
   163	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   164	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   165	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   166	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   167	-/
   168	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   169	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   170	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   171	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   172	
   173	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is a named
   174	Lean proof obligation for the prose assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`,
   175	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
   176	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   177	-/
   178	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   179	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   180	  sorry
   181	
   182	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is the
   183	level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   184	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   185	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   186	-/
   187	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   188	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   189	  sorry
   190	
   191	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   192	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   193	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   194	-/
   195	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   196	
   197	/-- The support of the typed CL question distribution, obtained by pushing a
   198	uniform seed through the type-indexed maps.  This is the construction in
   199	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   200	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   201	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   202	-/
   203	noncomputable def ldQuestionSupport (P : LdParams) :
   204	    Finset (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   205	  (Finset.univ : Finset ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)).image (fun s =>
   206	    ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   207	
   208	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   209	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   210	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   211	-/
   212	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   213	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   214	  Distribution.map
   215	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   216	    (fun s =>
   217	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   218	
   219	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   220	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   221	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   222	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   223	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   224	-/
   225	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   226	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   227	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   228	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   229	  deriving DecidableEq
   230	
   231	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   232	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   233	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   234	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   235	-/
   236	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   237	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   238	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   239	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   240	
   241	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   242	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   243	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   244	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   245	-/
   246	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   247	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   248	  toFun
   249	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   250	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   251	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   252	  invFun
   253	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   254	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   255	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   256	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   257	  right_inv := by
   258	    intro x
   259	    cases x with
   260	    | inl a => rfl
   261	    | inr x =>
   262	        cases x with
   263	        | inl a => rfl
   264	        | inr a => rfl
   265	
   266	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   267	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   268	
   269	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   270	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   271	
   272	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   273	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   274	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   275	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   276	-/
   277	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   278	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   279	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   280	
   281	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   282	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   283	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   284	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   285	-/
   286	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   287	  match t, a with
   288	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   289	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   290	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   291	  | _, _ => false
   292	
   293	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   294	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   295	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   296	-/
   297	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   298	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   299	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   300	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   301	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   302	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   303	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   304	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   305	
   306	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   307	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   308	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   309	-/
   310	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   311	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   312	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   313	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   314	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   315	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   316	
   317	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   318	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   319	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   320	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   321	-/
   322	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   323	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   324	  open Classical in
   325	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   326	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   327	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   328	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   329	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   330	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   331	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   332	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   333	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   334	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   335	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   336	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   337	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   338	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   339	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   340	      else false
   341	
   342	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   343	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   344	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   345	-/
   346	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   347	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   348	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   349	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   350	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   351	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   352	  μ_prob := by sorry
   353	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   354	
   355	end
   356	
   357	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import Mathlib
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.Pauli

     7	/-!
     8	# Pauli basis test soundness
     9	
    10	The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
    11	here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
    12	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
    13	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    20	The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
    21	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    27	
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    29	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    30	
    31	noncomputable section
    32	
    33	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    34	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    35	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
    36	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    39	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    40	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    41	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    42	
    43	/-- Matrix conjugation by a finite-dimensional linear isometry.  This is a
    44	Lean-only helper for the operator conclusion of `thm:pauli`; it uses the
    45	matrix representation of the isometry and its conjugate transpose.  Blueprint
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    50	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    51	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    52	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    53	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    54	  U * M * Uᴴ
    55	
    56	/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence.  This is the
    57	coordinate form of the tensor-register shuffle used in the paper's ideal
    58	state (`def:EPR`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`),
    59	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
    60	-/
    61	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    62	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    63	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    64	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    65	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    66	
    67	/-- Coordinate tensoring of two local maps on a bipartite state.  The formula
    68	is a genuine finite sum over the input coordinates; preservation of the norm
    69	is part of the later soundness proof for `thm:pauli`, blueprint
    70	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    71	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    72	-/
    73	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    74	    {ιA ιB ιA' ιB' R : Type*}
    75	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    76	    [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA'] [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    77	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    78	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × R))
    79	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × R))
    80	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    81	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) :=
    82	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) ℂ).symm
    83	    (fun p =>
    84	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    85	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × R) ℂ)
    86	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    87	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιB' × R) ℂ)
    88	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    89	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)) )
    90	
    91	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    92	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    93	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper
    94	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    95	-/
    96	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    97	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    98	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    99	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
   100	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   101	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
   102	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
   103	    (fun p =>
   104	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
   105	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
   106	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
   107	
   108	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
   109	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   110	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
   111	-/
   112	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
   113	  (.pauli W, 0)
   114	
   115	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
   116	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
   117	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
   119	-/
   120	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   121	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   122	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   123	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   124	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   125	  fun p q =>
   126	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
   127	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
   128	    else 0
   129	
   130	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
   131	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   133	-/
   134	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   135	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   136	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   137	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   138	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   139	  fun p q =>
   140	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
   141	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
   142	    else 0
   143	
   144	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   145	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   146	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   147	-/
   148	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   149	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   150	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   151	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   152	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   153	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   154	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   155	  fun p q =>
   156	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   157	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   158	    else 0
   159	
   160	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   161	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   162	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   163	-/
   164	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   165	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   166	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   167	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   168	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   169	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   170	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   171	  fun p q =>
   172	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   173	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   174	    else 0
   175	
   176	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   177	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   178	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   179	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   180	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   181	-/
   182	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   183	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   184	  ιA' : Type
   185	  ιB' : Type
   186	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   187	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   188	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   189	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   190	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   191	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   192	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   193	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   194	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   195	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   196	
   197	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   198	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   199	
   200	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   201	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   202	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   203	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   204	-/
   205	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   206	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   207	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   208	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   209	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   210	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   211	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   212	
   213	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   214	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   215	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   216	-/
   217	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   218	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   219	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   220	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   221	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   222	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   223	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   224	
   225	/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
   226	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   227	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
   228	once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
   229	each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.
   230	Blueprint
   231	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper origin
   232	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   233	
   234	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   235	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   236	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
   237	-/
   238	theorem pauli_soundness :
   239	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   240	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   241	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   242	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   243	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   244	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   245	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   246	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   247	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   248	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   249	  sorry
   250	
   251	end
   252	
   253	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

 "body": "### Motivation\n\n- Repair the 17 findings from the round-1 review of local issue #0006, published\n  as GitHub issue #4, for the QPBT statement skeleton.\n- Restore the source-facing definitions to the Pauli basis test and its\n  definition closure.  The primary sources are\n  `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:231-384,433-502,653-728,832-897,946-1161`,\n  `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57,219-230,258-271`,\n  `references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`, and\n  `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391,512-610,908-1225,1426-1447`.\n\n### Description\n\n- Encode `FixedFieldModel` with an actual `ZMod 2` algebra, a basis, its\n  self-duality and normality witnesses, and derive the binary representation\n  from the basis coordinates.  The model is fixed in `AdmissibleParams`, as the\n  paper requires; no fresh field identification is added to `pauli_soundness`.\n- Define `tauObservable` independently from the single-qudit shift and phase\n  operators, retaining the Fourier expansion identities as proof obligations.\n- Correct conditional-linear concatenation, require nonempty graph support,\n  remove the unused low-degree edge set, and provide the proved Magic Square\n  nonemptiness witness.\n- Correct Point/Pair orientation, add both supported Magic Square orientations,\n  make same-type consistency unconditional, and accept unsupported total cases\n  as prescribed by the decider.\n- Use `Matrix.toEuclideanLin` for the shared Hilbert-space action and the\n  state-dependent operator distances; allow the source's `epsilon = 0` boundary.\n- Add the missing helper docstrings and replace stale paper anchors.  Blueprint\n  links are intentionally unchanged in this repair; the known missing `\\\\uses`\n  edges and QPBT chapter links are tracked for the Stage 4.2 synchronization.\n\nAll remaining `sorry`s are proof-level obligations explicitly allowed by the\nStage 4.1 skeleton brief; no definition body or axiom was added.  The fixed\nbasis fields are source-facing data, while the finite serialization equivalence\nand Euclidean coordinate helpers are Lean-only representation infrastructure.\n\n### Statement Integrity\n\n- **Paper assumptions:** admissible `q = 2^k` with odd `k`, `m | q`, a fixed\n  self-dual normal field representation, and a finite-dimensional tensor-product\n  strategy passing the Pauli basis test with probability at least `1 - epsilon`.\n- **Lean assumptions:** `AdmissibleParams` carries `q`, `m`, `d`, the admissibility\n  and divisibility proofs, and the fixed `FixedFieldModel` basis/algebra data;\n  `Strategy` carries finite Euclidean registers and a unit state; the theorem\n  assumes `0 <= epsilon` and the same success inequality.  These are faithful\n  finite-type and boundary hypotheses, not a residual or repair package.\n- **Paper conclusion:** universal constants and a quantitative error scale,\n  local isometries into auxiliary registers tensored with Pauli registers, a\n  unit auxiliary state, and state-dependent closeness of the state and both\n  Pauli POVM families.\n- **Lean conclusion:** existential `a,b` with the stated bounds and a\n  `PauliSoundnessWitness` containing finite auxiliary types, local isometries,\n  and a unit auxiliary vector; it states the Euclidean state inequality and the\n  two explicit squared operator-distance inequalities using `deltaQld`.\n- **Verdict:** faithful finite-dimensional encoding with ordinary typeclass and\n  nonemptiness boundary hypotheses.  No extra bridge, residual, producer, or\n  assumptions bundle is present.  The analytic arguments remain intentional\n  Stage 4.1 proof obligations, and the explicit inequalities make the paper's\n  asymptotic distance convention concrete.\n\n### Testing\n\n- `lake env lean` passed for all twelve edited QPBT modules in dependency order.\n- `git diff --check` and the QPBT line-length audit passed.\n- The proof-hole scan reports only the intentional Stage 4.1 `sorry` sites; no\n  `axiom`, `native_decide`, or kernel-bypass declaration was introduced.\n- The repository pre-commit statement-integrity, proof-debt, faithful-boundary,\n  and conclusion-shaped-hypothesis checks all passed.\n- The direct full build was attempted, but this repair worktree's copied package\n  source cache is incomplete; the authoritative local CI gate is run separately\n  through `local/bin/ci.sh` with the hot cache.\n\n---\nAddresses #4\n",

Instructions for coding agents working in `MIPStarRE`. This is the **single
source of truth** for agent conventions. Claude Code agents should also read
`CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific notes.

## Project Overview

This repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics
around $MIP^* = RE$. It is the **local-only continuation** of
[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is
the **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active
track is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\*=RE*
(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and *NEEXP in MIP\** (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).

CI, review, and auto-fix **execute locally**; issues, PRs, their evidence and
merges live on GitHub (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`), reached only through
`local/bin/gh_common.py`. Read `local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before
doing workflow actions; the `## Local Operations` section below summarizes the
rules.

Key locations:

- `references/qpbt-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of MIP\*=RE
  (arXiv:2001.04383); the QPBT lives in
  `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` and
  `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`
- `references/neexp-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of NEEXP in MIP\*
  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source
  (`07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex`)
- `references/ldt-paper/` — in-repo TeX source mirror for LDT
- `blueprint/src/` — active LaTeX blueprint with Lean cross-references
  (`\lean{}`, `\leanok`)
- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint
- `audits/` — dated audit reports, scouting notes, and repair plans
- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — the local workflow layer

A legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.

**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):

1. `references/` paper mirrors — TeX source of the papers
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/` — active LaTeX blueprint
3. `MIPStarRE/` — Lean scaffold

Always read the paper source before formalizing or proving a statement. The
paper contains the precise mathematical definitions, theorem statements, and
proof strategies that the Lean code must faithfully represent. When stuck on a
sorry site or proof, go back to the original paper TeX source — the answer is
almost always there. Do not guess or try random tactics without first
understanding the paper's proof strategy.

## Repository Layout

```
MIPStarRE/
├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure
│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...
│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types
└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)
    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements
    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem
    ├── Preliminaries/
    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/
    ├── MainInductionStep/
    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/
    ├── GlobalVariance/
    ├── SelfImprovement/
    ├── CommutativityPoints/
    ├── Commutativity/
    └── Pasting/
```

Each LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports
flow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.

## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands

Run commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.

### First-time setup

```bash
lake exe cache get
lake build
scripts/install_git_hooks.sh
scripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check
```

Run the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks
move fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync
checks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.

### Full project build (CI-equivalent)

```bash
lake build
```

### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)

```bash
lake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean
```

### Check for proof holes in one file

```bash
rg -n "sorry|axiom" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true
```

### Check for proof holes in the whole project

```bash
rg -n "sorry|axiom" MIPStarRE
```

### Declaration checker

```bash
lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls
```

Use this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.

### Blueprint build

```bash
leanblueprint pdf    # PDF output
leanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)
```

In CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.

### What counts as a single test

This repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest
single-test commands are:

- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and
  `rg -n "sorry|axiom" path/to/File.lean || true`
- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`
- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and
  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`

### Recommended validation sequence

For a Lean file change:

1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`
2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`
3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`

For blueprint changes:

1. Run `leanblueprint web`
2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`

## Toolchain

- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)
- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)

Important `lakefile.toml` options:

- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly
- `pp.unicode.fun = true`
- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`
- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`

## Proof-Filling Order

Sections must be filled in this dependency order:

1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries
2. Section 5: making measurements projective
3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance
4. Section 9: self-improvement
5. Sections 10–11: commutativity
6. Section 12: pasting
7. Section 6: main induction wrapper

Do not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.

## Faithful Formalization Policy

A declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean
statement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.
Changing a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in
`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a
faithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.
This applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper
result, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the
hypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose
conclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra
load-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not
the paper theorem.
The project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize
them as permanent infrastructure.

If the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must
not mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either
leave the source-labelled entry without `\leanok`, or state the restricted or
conditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are
displayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\leanok` only
against a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must
not be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.

When a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a
source theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.
The note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of
the cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,
deriving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.

This rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as
`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked
from the blueprint by `\lean{...}` and `\leanok`.

Before editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,
`prop:*`):

1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.
2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are
   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.
3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer
   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary
   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.
4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named
   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.
5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A
   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it
   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains
   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem
   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its
   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like
   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example
   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a
   name ending in `_ofObligations`.
6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper
   with `\leanok`.

When reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package
hypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction
and turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not
actually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as
a strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave
the missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a
tracked `sorry` during a repair PR.

Some side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a
division, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model
instances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of
assumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and
documented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is
different: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such
as a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,
`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the
paper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions
should not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;
they require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.

    32	def registerSubmodule (K : Type*) [Field K] (S : Finset ι) : Submodule K (ι → K) :=
    33	  Submodule.span K {v | ∃ i, i ∈ S ∧ v = Pi.single i 1}
    34	
    35	/--
    36	`dotOrthogonal W` consists of vectors whose coordinate dot product with every
    37	member of `W` vanishes.  This is `def:dot-product-orthogonal` in
    38	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:31-42`, with paper origin
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:241-255`.

    41	def dotOrthogonal (W : Submodule K (ι → K)) : Submodule K (ι → K) where
    42	  carrier := {u | ∀ v, v ∈ W → dotProduct u v = 0}
    43	  zero_mem' := by

    45	    simp [dotProduct]
    46	  add_mem' := by
    47	    intro u v hu hv w hw
    48	    calc
    49	      dotProduct (u + v) w =
    50	          (dotProduct u w) + (dotProduct v w) := by
    51	            change (∑ i, (u i + v i) * w i) =
    52	              (∑ i, u i * w i) + (∑ i, v i * w i)
    53	            simp_rw [add_mul]
    54	            rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    55	      _ = 0 := by rw [hu w hw, hv w hw, add_zero]
    56	  smul_mem' := by
    57	    intro c u hu v hv
    58	    calc
    59	      dotProduct (c • u) v = c * dotProduct u v := by
    60	        simp [dotProduct, smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc, Finset.mul_sum]
    61	      _ = 0 := by rw [hu v hv, mul_zero]
    62

    65	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:84-110`, paper `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:231-384`.

   270	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   271	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   272	  let lineEdges :=
   273	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   274	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   275	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   276	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   277	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   278	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   279	  let basisEdges :=
   280	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   281	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   282	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   283	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))

   347	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are

   354	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   355	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   356	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)

   361	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   362	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   363	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin

   366	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   367	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   368	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   369	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   370	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   371	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))

   373	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   374	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   375	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   376	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   377	-/
   378	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   379	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   380	  toFun
   381	    | .value a => .inl a
   382	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   383	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   384	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   385	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   386	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   387	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   388	  invFun
   389	    | .inl a => .value a
   390	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   391	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   392	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   393	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   394	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   395	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   396	  left_inv := by
   397	    intro x
   398	    cases x <;> rfl
   399	  right_inv := by
   400	    intro x
   401	    cases x with
   402	    | inl a => rfl
   403	    | inr x =>
   404	        cases x with
   405	        | inl a => rfl
   406	        | inr x =>
   407	            cases x with
   408	            | inl a => rfl
   409	            | inr x =>
   410	                cases x with
   411	                | inl a => rfl
   412	                | inr x =>
   413	                    cases x with
   414	                    | inl a => rfl
   415	                    | inr x =>
   416	                        cases x with
   417	                        | inl a => rfl
   418	                        | inr a => rfl

   426	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   427	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   428	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   429	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   430	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   431	-/
   432	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   433	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   434	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   435	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   436	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   437	
   438	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   439	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   440	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   441	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   442	-/
   443	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   444	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   445	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   446	
   447	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   448	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   449	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   450	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   451	-/
   452	def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   453	  match t, a with
   454	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   455	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   456	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   457	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   458	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   459	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   460	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   461	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   462	  | _, _ => false
   463	
   464	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   465	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   466	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   467	-/
   468	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   469	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   470	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   471	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   472	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   473	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   474	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   475	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   476	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   477	
   478	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   479	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   480	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   481	-/
   482	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   483	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   484	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   485	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   486	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   487	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   488	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   489	
   490	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   491	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   492	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

   494	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   495	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   496	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   497	
   498	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   499	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   500	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   501	-/
   502	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   503	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   504	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   505	    (match W with
   506	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   507	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   508	
   509	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   510	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   511	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   512	-/
   513	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   514	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   515	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   516	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   517	      (a * (match W with
   518	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   519	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   520	
   521	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   522	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   523	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   524	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   525	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   526	-/
   527	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   528	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   529	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   530	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   531	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   532	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   533	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   534	
   535	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   536	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   537	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   538	-/
   539	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   540	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   541	  open Classical in
   542	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   543	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   544	      if tA = tB then
   545	        decide (a = b)
   546	      else
   547	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   548	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   550	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   552	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   553	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   554	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   555	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   556	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   557	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   558	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   559	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   560	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   561	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   562	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   564	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   565	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   566	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   567	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   568	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   569	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   570	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   571	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   572	          else true
   573	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   574	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   575	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   576	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   577	          else true
   578	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   579	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   580	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   581	          else true
   582	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   583	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   584	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   585	          else true
   586	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   587	    else false

   590	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   591	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   592	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   593	-/
   594	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   595	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   596	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   597	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   598	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   599	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   600	  μ_prob := by sorry
   601	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P

   603	end

     7	
     8	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     9	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
    10	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    11	carrier is needed here.

    15	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from

    24	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    25	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    27	-/
    28	inductive MsType where
    29	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    30	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    31	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    32	
    33	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    34	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    36	-/
    37	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    38	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    39	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    40	
    41	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    42	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    43	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    44	-/
    45	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    46	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    47	
    48	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    49	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    51	-/
    52	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    53	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    54	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    55	
    56	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    57	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    58	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    59	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    60	-/
    61	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    62	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    63	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    64	
    65	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    66	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    67	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    68	-/
    69	inductive MsAnswer where
    70	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    71	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    72	  deriving DecidableEq
    73	
    74	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    75	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint

    77	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.

    79	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    80

    82	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    83	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    87	  toFun
    88	    | .triple β => .inl β
    89	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    90	  invFun
    91	    | .inl β => .triple β
    92	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    93	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    94	  right_inv := by
    95	    intro x
    96	    cases x <;> rfl
    97

    99	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm

   103	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   104	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   106	-/
   107	def msWinPredicate :
   108	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   109	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   110	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   111	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   112	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   113	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   114	      decide
   115	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   116	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   117	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   118	      decide
   119	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   120	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   121	  | _, _, _, _ => false

   125	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   128	  QuestionA := MsType
   129	  QuestionB := MsType
   130	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   131	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   132	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   133	  μ_prob := by sorry
   134	  decide := msWinPredicate

   299	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   300	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   301	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   302	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   303	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   304	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   305	
   306	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   307	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   308	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   309	-/
   310	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   311	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   312	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   313	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   314	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   315	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   316	
   317	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   318	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   319	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   320	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   321	-/
   322	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   323	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   324	  open Classical in
   325	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   326	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   327	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   328	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   329	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   330	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   331	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   332	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   333	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   334	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   335	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   336	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   337	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   338	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   339	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   340	      else false
   341	
   342	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   343	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   344	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   345	-/
   346	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   347	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   348	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   349	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   350	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   351	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   352	  μ_prob := by sorry
   353	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   354	
   355	end
   356	
   357	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    11	here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
    12	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
    13	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    14

    17	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin

    31	noncomputable section
    32	
    33	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    34	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    35	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
    36	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    39	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    40	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    41	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    42	
    43	/-- Matrix conjugation by a finite-dimensional linear isometry.  This is a
    44	Lean-only helper for the operator conclusion of `thm:pauli`; it uses the
    45	matrix representation of the isometry and its conjugate transpose.  Blueprint
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    50	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    51	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    52	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    53	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    54	  U * M * Uᴴ
    55	
    56	/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence.  This is the
    57	coordinate form of the tensor-register shuffle used in the paper's ideal
    58	state (`def:EPR`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`),
    59	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
    60	-/
    61	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    62	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    63	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    64	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    65	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    66	
    67	/-- Coordinate tensoring of two local maps on a bipartite state.  The formula
    68	is a genuine finite sum over the input coordinates; preservation of the norm
    69	is part of the later soundness proof for `thm:pauli`, blueprint
    70	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    71	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    72	-/
    73	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    74	    {ιA ιB ιA' ιB' R : Type*}
    75	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    76	    [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA'] [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    77	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    78	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × R))
    79	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × R))
    80	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    81	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) :=
    82	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) ℂ).symm
    83	    (fun p =>
    84	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    85	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × R) ℂ)
    86	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    87	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιB' × R) ℂ)
    88	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    89	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)) )
    90	
    91	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    92	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    93	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper
    94	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    95	-/
    96	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    97	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    98	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    99	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
   100	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   101	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
   102	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
   103	    (fun p =>
   104	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
   105	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
   106	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
   107	
   108	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
   109	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   110	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
   111	-/
   112	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
   113	  (.pauli W, 0)
   114	
   115	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
   116	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
   117	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
   119	-/
   120	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   121	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   122	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   123	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   124	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   125	  fun p q =>
   126	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
   127	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
   128	    else 0
   129	
   130	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
   131	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   133	-/
   134	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   135	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   136	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   137	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   138	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   139	  fun p q =>
   140	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
   141	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
   142	    else 0
   143	
   144	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   145	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   146	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   147	-/
   148	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   149	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   150	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   151	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   152	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   153	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   154	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   155	  fun p q =>
   156	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   157	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   158	    else 0

   161	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   162	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.

   164	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   165	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   166	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   167	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   168	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   169	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   170	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   171	  fun p q =>
   172	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   173	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   174	    else 0

   176	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   177	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   178	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   179	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   180	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.

   182	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   183	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   184	  ιA' : Type
   185	  ιB' : Type
   186	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   187	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   188	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   189	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   190	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   191	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   192	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   193	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   194	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   195	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   196	
   197	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   198	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   199	
   200	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   201	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   202	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   203	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   204	-/
   205	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   206	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   207	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   208	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   209	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   210	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   211	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   212	
   213	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   214	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   215	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   216	-/
   217	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   218	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   219	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   220	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   221	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   222	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   223	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2

   226	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   227	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
   228	once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for

   234	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   235	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   236	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
   237	-/
   238	theorem pauli_soundness :
   239	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   240	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   241	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   242	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,

   244	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   245	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   246	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   247	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   248	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   249	  sorry
   250	
   251	end

   253	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

The analytic arguments remain intentional\n  Stage 4.1 proof obligations, and the explicit inequalities make the paper's\n  asymptotic distance convention concrete.\n\n### Testing\n\n- `lake env lean` passed for all twelve edited QPBT modules in dependency order.\n- `git diff --check` and the QPBT line-length audit passed.\n- The proof-hole scan reports only the intentional Stage 4.1 `sorry` sites; no\n  `axiom`, `native_decide`, or kernel-bypass declaration was introduced.\n- The repository pre-commit statement-integrity, proof-debt, faithful-boundary,\n  and conclusion-shaped-hypothesis checks all passed.\n- The direct full build was attempted, but this repair worktree's copied package\n  source cache is incomplete; the authoritative local CI gate is run separately\n  through `local/bin/ci.sh` with the hot cache.\n\n---\nAddresses #4\n",
