     6	/-!
     7	# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value
     8	
     9	This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
    10	states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
    11	`Measurement` structure.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
    16	`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
    18	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/--
    29	A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
    30	pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
    31	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Game where
    35	  QuestionA : Type
    36	  QuestionB : Type
    37	  AnswerA : Type
    38	  AnswerB : Type
    39	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
    40	  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
    41	  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
    42	  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
    43	  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
    44	  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
    45	  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
    46	  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
    47	  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
    48	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    49	  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool
    50	
    51	attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
    52	  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
    53	  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
    54	
    55	/--
    56	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    57	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    58	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
    59	is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    61	-/
    62	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    63	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    64	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    65	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
    66	  M.postprocess Prod.fst
    67	
    68	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
    69	`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
    70	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    71	-/
    72	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    73	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]

    25	/--

    28	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    29	-/
    30	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    31	    [DecidableEq ι]
    32	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    33	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    34	
    35	/--
    36	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    37	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,

    41	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    42	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    43	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=

    14	## References
    15

    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    27	
    28	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    29	
    30	/--
    31	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    32	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    33	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    34	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    35	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    36	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    37	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`,
    38	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    39	-/
    40	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    41	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    42	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    43	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    44	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    45	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    46	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    47	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    48	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    49	
    50	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    51	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    52	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`, paper origin
    53	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    54	-/
    55	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    56	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    57	
    58	/-- Evaluation of a conditionally-linear syntax term.  Lean-only support for
    59	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    61	-/
    62	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    63	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    64	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    65	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    66	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    67	      fun x =>
    68	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    69	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    70	
    71	/-- The support invariant for a conditionally-linear syntax term.  This is a
    72	Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    73	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    74	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    75	-/
    76	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    77	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    78	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    79	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    80	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    81	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    82	
    83	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    84	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    87	-/
    88	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    89	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    90	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    91	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    92	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
    93	
    94	/--
    95	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
    96	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`; paper
    97	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    98	-/
    99	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
   100	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
   101	
   102	/--
   103	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   104	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:467-470`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   107	-/
   108	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   109	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   110	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   111	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   112	
   113	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   114	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   115	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   116	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   117	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, paper origin
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   119	-/
   120	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   121	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   122	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   123	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   124	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   125	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   126	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   127	
   128	/--
   129	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   130	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, with
   131	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   132	The direct-sum coordinate bookkeeping is represented by `condLinearConcat`; the
   133	level proof remains deferred in this skeleton.
   134	-/
   135	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   136	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   137	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   138	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   139	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   140	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   141	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   142	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   143	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   144	  sorry
   145	
   146	/--
   147	The graph distribution samples an ordered endpoint pair whose unordered edge
   148	`s(a,b)` lies in `E`, including self-loops.  It is the inlined graph sampler of
   149	`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:553-563`;
   150	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   151	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   153	-/
   154	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   155	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   156	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   157	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   158	
   159	/-- The graph sampler has unit mass whenever its edge set is nonempty. -/
   160	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   161	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   162	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   163	  sorry

     5	/-!
     6	# The Magic Square game
     7	
     8	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     9	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
    10	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    11	carrier is needed here.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    25	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    27	-/
    28	inductive MsType where
    29	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    30	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    31	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    32	
    33	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    34	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    36	-/
    37	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    38	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    39	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    40	
    41	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    42	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    43	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    44	-/
    45	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    46	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    47	
    48	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    49	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    51	-/
    52	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    53	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    54	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    55	
    56	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    57	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    58	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    59	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    60	-/
    61	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    62	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    63	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    64	
    65	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    66	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    67	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    68	-/
    69	inductive MsAnswer where
    70	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    71	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    72	  deriving DecidableEq
    73	
    74	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    75	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    76	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    78	-/
    79	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    80	
    81	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    82	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    83	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    87	  toFun
    88	    | .triple β => .inl β
    89	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    90	  invFun
    91	    | .inl β => .triple β
    92	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    93	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    94	  right_inv := by
    95	    intro x
    96	    cases x <;> rfl
    97	
    98	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
    99	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
   100	
   101	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
   102	
   103	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   104	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   106	-/
   107	def msWinPredicate :
   108	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   109	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   110	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   111	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   112	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   113	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   114	      decide
   115	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   116	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   117	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   118	      decide
   119	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   120	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   121	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   122	
   123	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   124	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   125	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   128	  QuestionA := MsType
   129	  QuestionB := MsType
   130	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   131	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   132	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   133	  μ_prob := by sorry
   134	  decide := msWinPredicate
   135	
   136	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   225	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where

   231	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   232	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   233	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   234	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   235	-/
   236	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   237	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   238	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   239	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   240	
   241	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   242	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   243	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   244	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   245	-/
   246	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   247	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   248	  toFun
   249	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   250	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   251	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   252	  invFun
   253	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   254	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   255	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   256	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   257	  right_inv := by
   258	    intro x
   259	    cases x with
   260	    | inl a => rfl
   261	    | inr x =>
   262	        cases x with
   263	        | inl a => rfl
   264	        | inr a => rfl
   265	
   266	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   267	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   268	
   269	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   270	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   271	
   272	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   273	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   274	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   275	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   276	-/
   277	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   278	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   279	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   280	
   281	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   282	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   283	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   284	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   285	-/
   286	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   287	  match t, a with
   288	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   289	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   290	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   291	  | _, _ => false
   292	
   293	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   294	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   295	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   296	-/
   297	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   298	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   299	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   300	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   301	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   302	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   303	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   304	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   305	
   306	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   307	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   308	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   309	-/
   310	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   311	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   312	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   313	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   314	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   315	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   316	
   317	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   318	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   319	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   320	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   321	-/
   322	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   323	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   324	  open Classical in
   325	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   326	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   327	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   328	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   329	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   330	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   331	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   332	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   333	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   334	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   335	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   336	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   337	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   338	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   339	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   340	      else false
   341	
   342	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   343	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   344	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   345	-/
   346	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   347	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   348	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   349	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   350	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   351	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   352	  μ_prob := by sorry
   353	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   354	
   355	end

   357	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   270	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=

   272	  let lineEdges :=

   289	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>

   317	/-- The finite support obtained by sampling an edge and a common ambient seed,

   347	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are

   351	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where

   353	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   354	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   355	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   356	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   357	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   358	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   359	  deriving DecidableEq

   361	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   362	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   363	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   364	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

   366	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   367	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   368	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   369	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   370	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   371	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   372	
   373	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   374	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   375	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   376	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   377	-/
   378	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   379	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   380	  toFun
   381	    | .value a => .inl a
   382	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   383	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   384	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   385	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   386	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   387	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   388	  invFun
   389	    | .inl a => .value a
   390	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   391	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   392	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   393	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   394	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   395	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   396	  left_inv := by
   397	    intro x
   398	    cases x <;> rfl
   399	  right_inv := by
   400	    intro x
   401	    cases x with
   402	    | inl a => rfl
   403	    | inr x =>
   404	        cases x with
   405	        | inl a => rfl
   406	        | inr x =>
   407	            cases x with
   408	            | inl a => rfl
   409	            | inr x =>
   410	                cases x with
   411	                | inl a => rfl
   412	                | inr x =>
   413	                    cases x with
   414	                    | inl a => rfl
   415	                    | inr x =>
   416	                        cases x with
   417	                        | inl a => rfl
   418	                        | inr a => rfl

   420	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
   421	  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm

   492	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   493	-/
   494	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   495	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   496	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   497	
   498	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   499	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   500	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   501	-/
   502	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   503	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   504	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   505	    (match W with
   506	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   507	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   508	
   509	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   510	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   511	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   512	-/
   513	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   514	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   515	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   516	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   517	      (a * (match W with
   518	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   519	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   520	
   521	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   522	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   523	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   524	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   525	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   526	-/
   527	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   528	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   529	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   530	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   531	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   532	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   533	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   534	
   535	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   536	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   537	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   538	-/
   539	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   540	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   541	  open Classical in
   542	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   543	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   544	      if tA = tB then
   545	        decide (a = b)
   546	      else
   547	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   548	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   550	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   552	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   553	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   554	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   555	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   556	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   557	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   558	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   559	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   560	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   561	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   562	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   564	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   565	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   566	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   567	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   568	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   569	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   570	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   571	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   572	          else true
   573	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   574	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   575	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   576	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   577	          else true
   578	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   579	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   580	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   581	          else true
   582	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   583	          if (W = .X ∧ j = ⟨0, by decide⟩) ∨ (W = .Z ∧ j = ⟨4, by decide⟩) then
   584	            decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   585	          else true
   586	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   587	    else false
   588	
   589	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   590	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   591	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   592	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   593	-/
   594	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   595	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   596	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   597	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   598	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   599	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   600	  μ_prob := by sorry
   601	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   602	
   603	end
   604	
   605	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     8	# Pauli basis test soundness
     9	
    10	The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
    11	here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
    12	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
    13	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    20	The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
    21	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    27

    29	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    30	
    31	noncomputable section
    32	
    33	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    34	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    35	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
    36	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    39	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    40	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    41	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    42	
    43	/-- Matrix conjugation by a finite-dimensional linear isometry.  This is a
    44	Lean-only helper for the operator conclusion of `thm:pauli`; it uses the
    45	matrix representation of the isometry and its conjugate transpose.  Blueprint
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    50	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    51	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    52	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    53	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    54	  U * M * Uᴴ
    55	
    56	/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence.  This is the
    57	coordinate form of the tensor-register shuffle used in the paper's ideal
    58	state (`def:EPR`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`),
    59	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
    60	-/
    61	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    62	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    63	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    64	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    65	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    66	
    67	/-- Coordinate tensoring of two local maps on a bipartite state.  The formula
    68	is a genuine finite sum over the input coordinates; preservation of the norm
    69	is part of the later soundness proof for `thm:pauli`, blueprint
    70	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    71	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    72	-/
    73	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    74	    {ιA ιB ιA' ιB' R : Type*}
    75	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    76	    [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA'] [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    77	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    78	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × R))
    79	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × R))
    80	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    81	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) :=
    82	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) ℂ).symm
    83	    (fun p =>
    84	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    85	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × R) ℂ)
    86	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    87	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιB' × R) ℂ)
    88	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    89	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)) )
    90	
    91	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    92	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    93	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper
    94	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    95	-/
    96	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    97	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    98	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    99	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
   100	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   101	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
   102	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
   103	    (fun p =>
   104	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
   105	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
   106	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
   107	
   108	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
   109	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   110	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
   111	-/
   112	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
   113	  (.pauli W, 0)
   114	
   115	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
   116	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
   117	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
   119	-/
   120	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   121	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   122	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   123	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   124	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   125	  fun p q =>
   126	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
   127	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
   128	    else 0
   129	
   130	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
   131	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   133	-/
   134	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   135	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   136	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   137	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   138	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   139	  fun p q =>
   140	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
   141	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
   142	    else 0
   143	
   144	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   145	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   146	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   147	-/
   148	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   149	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   150	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   151	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   152	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   153	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   154	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   155	  fun p q =>
   156	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   157	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   158	    else 0
   159	
   160	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   161	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   162	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   163	-/
   164	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   165	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   166	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   167	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   168	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   169	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   170	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   171	  fun p q =>
   172	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   173	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   174	    else 0
   175	
   176	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   177	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   178	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   179	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   180	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   181	-/
   182	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   183	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   184	  ιA' : Type
   185	  ιB' : Type
   186	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   187	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   188	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   189	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   190	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   191	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   192	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   193	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   194	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   195	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   196	
   197	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   198	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   199	
   200	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   201	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   202	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   203	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   204	-/
   205	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   206	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   207	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   208	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   209	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   210	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   211	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   212	
   213	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   214	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   215	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   216	-/
   217	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   218	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   219	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   220	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   221	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   222	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   223	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   224	
   225	/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
   226	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   227	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
   228	once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
   229	each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.
   230	Blueprint
   231	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper origin
   232	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   233	
   234	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   235	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   236	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
   237	-/
   238	theorem pauli_soundness :
   239	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   240	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   241	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   242	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   243	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   244	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   245	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   246	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   247	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   248	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   249	  sorry
   250	
   251	end
   252	
   253	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

900	\label{lem:ld-encoding-complexity}
   901	Let $q$ be an admissible field size, and let $M = 2^m$ for some integer $m$.
   902	The complexity of computing the evaluation of the low-degree encoding $g_a(x)$,
   903	given $a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$ represented in binary, is $\poly(M,\log
   904	q)$.
   905	\end{lemma}
   906	\begin{proof}
   907		Computing $g_a(x)$ requires computing the sum of products $a_y \cdot
   908	  \ind_{m,y}(x)$ over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$.
   909	  Via \Cref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}, evaluating $\ind_{m,y}(x)$ takes time
   910	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ because it requires performing $m$ multiplications of $\F_q$
   911	  elements, and therefore the product $a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)$ requires
   912	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ time.
   913	  Computing the sum over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ requires $M \cdot \poly(m,\log q)
   914	  = \poly(M,\log q)$ time, as claimed.
   915	\end{proof}
   916	
   917	Finally, for any $H \subseteq \F_q$ we define the \emph{decoding} map
   918	$\coded_H(\cdot)$ which takes as input a polynomial $g : \F_q^m \to \F_q$ and
   919	returns the following vector $a \in \F_q^M$: for all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, if $g(y)
   920	\in H$, then set $a_y = g(y)$, and otherwise set $a_y = 0$.
   921	Note that for all $a \in H^M$ we have $\coded_H(g_a) = a$ where $g_a$ is the
   922	low-degree encoding of $a$.
   923	For notational brevity we often write $\coded(\cdot)$ to denote the boolean
   924	decoding map $\coded_{\{0,1\}}(\cdot)$.

   926	\subsection{Linear spaces and registers}
   927	\label{sec:lin-reg}
   928	
   929	For a set $V$, we write $\C^V$ for the complex vector space of dimension $|V|$.
   930	The space $\C^V$ is endowed with a canonical orthonormal basis
   931	$\{\ket{x}\}_{x\in V}$.
   932	By ``a quantum state on $V$'' we mean a unit vector
   933	\begin{equation*}
   934	  \ket{\psi}_V \in \complex^V\;.
   935	\end{equation*}
   936	If $V = \bigoplus_{i=1}^k V_k$ is the direct sum of subspaces $V_k$ over $\F$,
   937	then $\complex^V$ can be identified with $\bigotimes_{i=1}^k
   938	\complex^{V_i}$, by the identification of $\ket{x_1 \oplus \dots \oplus
   939	  x_k}$ with $\ket{x_1} \otimes \dots \otimes \ket{x_k}$.
   940	As a special case, if $\{e_i\}$ is a basis of $V$ the decomposition $V =
   941	\bigoplus_{i=1}^k ( \F e_i)$ yields the tensor product decomposition $\C^V =
   942	\bigotimes_{i=1}^k \C^{\abs{\F}}$.
   943	We sometimes refer to the spaces $\C^{\abs{\F}}$ as the ``qudits'' of $\C^V$ (or
   944	of a state on it).
   945	
   946	\begin{definition}
   947	  \label{def:EPR}
   948	  For a linear space $V$ over a finite field $\F$, define the \EPR state on $\C^V
   949	  \otimes \C^V$ by
   950	  \begin{equation*}
   951	    \ket{\EPR}_V = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\abs{V}}} \sum_{x\in V}\ket {x}\otimes \ket{x}\;.
   952	  \end{equation*}
   953	  We also write $\ket{\EPR}_{\F_q}$ as $\ket{\EPR_q}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}$ as
   954	  $\ket{\EPR}$.
   955	\end{definition}

   957	\subsection{Measurements and observables}
   958	
   959	Quantum measurements are modeled as positive operator-valued
   960	measures (POVMs).
   961	A POVM consists of a set of positive semidefinite operators $\{ M_a \}_{a\in S}$
   962	indexed by outcomes $a\in S$ that satisfy the condition $\sum_a M_a = I$. If the latter condition is relaxed to $\sum_a M_a \leq I$ then we refer to $\{M_a\}$ as a \emph{sub-measurement}.
   963	We sometimes use the same letter $M$ to refer to the collection of operators
   964	defining the POVM.
   965	The probability that the measurement returns outcome $a$ on state $\ket{\psi}$
   966	is given by
   967	\begin{equation*}
   968	  \Pr(a) = \bra{\psi} M_a \ket{\psi}\;.
   969	\end{equation*}
   970	A POVM $M=\{M_a\}$ is said to be \emph{projective} if each operator $M_a$ is a
   971	projector ($M_a^2 = M_a$). This automatically implies that operators
   972	$M_a, M_b$ for distinct outcomes $a \neq b$ are orthogonal ($M_a M_b =
   973	M_b M_a = 0$). An \emph{observable} is a unitary matrix.
   974	A \emph{binary observable} is an observable $O$ such that $O^2 = \Id$, i.e.\ $O$
   975	has eigenvalues in $\{-1,1\}$.
   976	
   977	We follow the convention that subscripts of the measurement index
   978	the outcome and superscripts of the measurement are used to index different
   979	measurements.
   980	For example, we use $\{M^x_{a,\, b}\}$ to represent a measurement indexed by $x$
   981	whose outcome consists of two parts $a$ and $b$.
   982	In this case, by slightly abusing the notation, we use $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{M^x_b\}$
   983	to denote
   984	\begin{equation*}
   985	  M^x_a = \sum_b M^x_{a,\, b}\;, \quad M^x_b = \sum_a M^x_{a,\, b}\;.
   986	\end{equation*}
   987	For any $x$, $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{M^x_b\}$ are POVMs sometimes referred to as the
   988	``marginals'' of $\{M^x_{a,\, b}\}$.
   989	
   990	\begin{definition}
   991	  \label{def:bracket}
   992	  Let $\{M^x_a\}_{a\in A}$ be a family of POVMs indexed by $x\in \cal{X}$.
   993	  Let $f:A\to B$ be an arbitrary function.
   994	  We write $\bigl\{ M^x_{[f(\cdot)=b]} \bigr\}$ for the POVM derived from
   995	  $\{M^x_a\}$ by applying the function $f$ before returning the outcome.
   996	  More precisely,
   997	\begin{equation*}
   998	  M^x_{[f(\cdot) = b]} = \sum_{a : f(a)=b} M^x_a\;.
   999	\end{equation*}
  1000	If $b$ is not in the image of $f$, then we define $M^x_{[f(\cdot) = b]}$ to be
  1001	$0$. In cases where the outcome $a$ has a natural interpretation as a tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$ we sometimes slightly abuse notation and write $M^x_{[a_i=b]}$ for some $i\in \{1,\ldots,k\}$ to denote 
  1002	\[ M^x_{[a_i=b]} \,=\,\sum_{(a_1,\ldots,a_k):\,a_i=b} M^x_{(a_1,\ldots,a_k)}\;.\]
  1003	\end{definition}

  1052	\subsection{Generalized Pauli observables}
  1053	\label{sec:generalized-pauli}
  1054	
  1055	
  1056	For prime number $p$, the generalized Pauli operators over $\Fp$ are a
  1057	collection of observables indexed by a basis setting $X$ or $Z$ and an element
  1058	$a$ or $b$ of $\Fp$, with eigenvalues that are $p$-th roots of unity.
  1059	They are given by
  1060	\begin{equation}
  1061	  \label{eq:pauli-fp}
  1062	  \sigma^X(a) = \sum_{j \in \Fp} \ket{j + a} \bra{j}\qquad \text{and} \qquad
  1063	  \sigma^Z(b) = \sum_{j \in \Fp} \omega^{bj} \ket{j} \bra{j}\;,
  1064	\end{equation}
  1065	where $\omega = e^{\frac{2\pi i}{p}}$, and addition and multiplication are over
  1066	$\Fp$.
  1067	These observables obey the ``twisted commutation'' relations
  1068	\begin{equation}
  1069	  \label{eq:twisted-fp}
  1070	  \forall a,b\in\Fp\;,\qquad \sigma^X(a)\, \sigma^Z(b) =
  1071	  \omega^{-ab} \,\sigma^Z(b)\,\sigma^X(a)\;.
  1072	\end{equation}
  1073	Similarly, over a field $\Fq$ with $q$ a power of $p$, we can consider a set of generalized Pauli
  1074	operators, indexed by a basis setting $X$ or $Z$ and an element of $\Fq$ and
  1075	with eigenvalues that are $p$-th roots of unity.
  1076	For $a, b\in\Fq$ they are given by
  1077	\begin{equation*}
  1078	  \qp^X(a) = \sum_{j \in \Fq} \ket{j+a}\bra{j} \qquad \text{and} \qquad
  1079	  \qp^Z(b)= \sum_{j \in \Fq} \omega^{\tr(b j)} \ket{j}\bra{j}\;,
  1080	\end{equation*}
  1081	where addition and multiplication are over $\Fq$.
  1082	For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $a, a' \in \Fq$, and $b \in \Fp$, powers of these
  1083	observables obey the relations
  1084	\begin{equation*}\label{eq:pauli-product-power}
  1085	  \bigl(\qp^W(a)\qp^W(a')\bigr) = \qp^W(a+a') \qquad \text{and}
  1086	  \qquad \bigl( \qp^W(a) \bigr)^b = \qp^W(a b) \;.
  1087	\end{equation*}
  1088	In particular, since $pa=0$ for any $a\in \Fq$ we get that that $(\qp^W(a))^p =
  1089	I$ for any $a\in\Fq$.
  1090	The observables obey analogous ``twisted commutation'' relations
  1091	to~\eqref{eq:twisted-fp},
  1092	\begin{equation}
  1093	  \label{eq:twisted-fq}
  1094	  \forall a, b \in \Fq\;, \qquad \qp^X(a)\, \qp^Z(b) =
  1095	  \omega^{-\tr(a b)} \, \qp^Z(b)\, \qp^X(a)\;.
  1096	\end{equation}
  1097	It is clear from the definition that all of the $\qp^X$ operators commute with
  1098	each other, and similarly all the $\qp^Z$ operators commute with each other.
  1099	Thus, it is meaningful to speak of a common eigenbasis for all $\qp^X$
  1100	operators, and a common eigenbasis for all $\qp^Z$ operators.
  1101	The common eigenbasis for the $\qp^Z$ operators is the computational
  1102	basis $\{\ket{j}\}_{j \in \F_q}$.
  1103	To map this basis to the common eigenbasis of the $\qp^X$ operators, one can
  1104	apply the Fourier transform
  1105	\begin{equation}
  1106	  \label{eq:fourier-f}
  1107	  F \,=\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{q}} \sum_{a, b\in \Fq} \omega^{-\tr(ab)}
  1108	  \ket{a}\bra{b}\;.
  1109	\end{equation}
  1110	Explicitly, the eigenbases consist of the vectors $\ket{e_W}$ labeled by an
  1111	element $e \in \Fq$ and $W \in \{X, Z\}$, given by
  1112	\begin{equation*}
  1113	  \ket{e_X} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{q}} \sum_j \omega^{- \tr(e j)} \ket{j}\;, \qquad
  1114	  \ket{e_Z}   = \ket{e}\;.
  1115	\end{equation*}
  1116	We denote the POVM whose elements are projectors onto basis vectors of the
  1117	eigenbasis associated with the observables $\qp^W$ by $\{\qp^W_e\}_e$.
  1118	Then for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and $a\in \Fq$, the observables $\qp^W(a)$ can be
  1119	written as
  1120	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pauli-obs-proj-single}
  1121	  \qp^W(a) = \sum_{b \in \Fq} \omega^{\tr(a b)} \qp^W_b\;.
  1122	\end{equation}
  1123	
  1124	To invert this relation, we first quote the following useful Fourier fact.
  1125	\begin{lemma}[Fact 3.2 of \cite{NW19}]
  1126	  \label{lem:cancellation}
  1127	  Let $V$ be a subspace of $\F^k$. For all $v \not\in V^\perp$, 
  1128	  \begin{equation*}
  1129	    \E_{u \sim V} \omega^{\tr(u \cdot v)} = 0\;,
  1130	  \end{equation*}
  1131	  where the expectation is over a uniformly random vector $u$ from $V$.
  1132	\end{lemma}
  1133	
  1134	We may now invert~\Cref{eq:pauli-obs-proj-single}:
  1135	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pauli-inversion-0-single}
  1136	  \E_{a\in \F_q} \omega^{-\tr(ab)} \qp^W(a) = \sum_{b'\in \F_q} \E_{a\in \F_q}
  1137	  \omega^{\tr(a(b'-b))} \qp^W_{b'} = \qp^W_b\;,
  1138	\end{equation}
  1139	where the second step follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:cancellation}.
  1140	
  1141	For systems with many qudits, we will consider tensor products of the operators
  1142	$\qp^W$.
  1143	Slightly abusing notation, for $W \in \{X, Z\}$ and $a \in \Fq^n$ we denote by
  1144	$\qp^W(a)$ the tensor product $\qp^W(a_1) \ot \dots \ot \qp^W(a_n)$.
  1145	These obey the twisted commutation relations
  1146	\begin{equation*}
  1147	  \forall a,b\in \Fq^n,\qquad \qp^X(a)\, \qp^Z(b) \,=\, \omega^{-\tr (a \cdot
  1148	    b)}\, \qp^Z(b)\, \qp^X(a)\;,
  1149	\end{equation*}
  1150	where $a \cdot b = \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i b_i \in \Fq$.
  1151	For $W\in\{X,Z\}$ and $e \in \Fq^n$ define the eigenstates
  1152	\[ \ket{e_W} = \ket{(e_1)_W} \ot \dots \ot \ket{(e_n)_W}\;, \]
  1153	and associated rank-$1$ projectors $\qp^W_e$. Analogous versions of \Cref{eq:pauli-obs-proj-single}
  1154	and \Cref{eq:pauli-inversion-0-single} relate the multi-qubit observables
  1155	and projectors:
  1156	\begin{align}
  1157	  \qp^W(a) &= \sum_{b \in \Fq^n} \omega^{\tr(a \cdot b)}
  1158	  \qp^W_b\;, \label{eq:pauli-obs-proj} \\
  1159	    \E_{a\in \F_q^n} \omega^{-\tr(a \cdot b)} \qp^W(a) &= \sum_{b'\in \F_q^n} \E_{a\in \F_q^n}
  1160	  \omega^{\tr(a\cdot (b'-b))} \qp^W_{b'} = \qp^W_b\;. \label{eq:pauli-inversion-0}
  1161	\end{align}

   953	can be used to form a perfect strategy for the Magic Square game

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

  1169	    On input $(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice, \tvar_\bob, x_\bob, a_\alice, a_\bob)$,
  1170	    the decision procedure $\decider^\pauli$ performs the following checks for
  1171	    $w \in \AB$:
  1172	    \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,parsep=2pt]
  1173	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1174	      \label{item:same-type}
  1175	      If $\tvar_\alice = \tvar_\bob$, accept iff $a_\alice = a_\bob$.
  1176	
  1177	    \item (\textbf{Low-degree}).
  1178	      \label{item:low-degree}
  1179	      Let $\ldparams = (q,m,d,1)$. 
  1180	      \begin{enumerate}
  1181	      	\item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\ALine, W)$, accept if
  1182	      $\decider^\ld_{\ldparams}$ accepts $(\Point, x_w, \ALine, x_{\overline{w}}, a_w,
  1183	      a_{\overline{w}})$.
  1184	      	\item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\DLine, W)$, accept if
  1185	      $\decider^\ld_{\ldparams}$ accepts $(\Point, x_w, \DLine, x_{\overline{w}}, a_w,
  1186	      a_{\overline{w}})$.
  1187			\end{enumerate}
  1188	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1189	      \label{item:low-degree-consistency}
  1190	      If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\Pauli, W)$, accept if
  1191	      $g_{a_{\overline{w}}}(x_w) = a_w$, where $g_{a_{\overline{w}}}$ is
  1192	      the low-degree encoding of $a_{\overline{w}} \in \F_q^M$ defined in
  1193	      Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.
  1194	    \end{enumerate}
  1195	    In the remaining four cases, the decision procedure first computes the
  1196	    number
  1197	    \begin{equation}
  1198	      \label{eq:gamma-value}
  1199	      \gamma = \tr \bigl( (\ind_{m}(u_\xpt) \cdot r_\xpt) \cdot
  1200	      (\ind_{m}(u_\zpt) \cdot r_\zpt) \bigr)\;,
  1201	    \end{equation}
  1202	    where we recall the $\ind_{m}(\cdot)$ vector from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.
  1203	    \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,parsep=2pt]
  1204	      \setcounter{enumi}{3}
  1205	    \item (\textbf{Commutation check}).
  1206	      \label{item:commutation} If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} =
  1207	      \Pair$, accept if $a_w = \beta_W$ or $\gamma \neq 0$.
  1208	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1209	      \label{item:commutation-consistency} If $\tvar_w = (\Point,W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} =
  1210	      (\Pair,W)$, accept if $\tr (a_w r_W) = a_{\overline{w}}$ or $\gamma \neq 0$.
  1211	      
  1212	    \item (\textbf{Magic square check}).
  1213	      \label{item:magic-square} If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i,
  1214	      \tvar_{\overline{w}} = \Variable_j$, accept if $\gamma = 0$, or $a_w$
  1215	      satisfies constraint $\Constraint_i$ and $ \alpha_j = a_{\overline{w}}$.
  1216	
  1217	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1218	      \label{item:magic-square-consistency}
  1219	      If $\tvar_w = (\Point,W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = \Variable_j$, accept if
  1220	      $\gamma = 0$ or if $j = 1$, $W = X$, and $\tr(a_w r_\xpt) =
  1221	      a_{\overline{w}}$ or if $j = 5$, $W = Z$, and $\tr(a_w r_\zpt) =
  1222	      a_{\overline{w}}$.
  1223	    \end{enumerate}

   307	
   308	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   309	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   310	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   311	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   312	-/
   313	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   314	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   315	  simp [pauliEdges]
   316	
   317	/-- The finite support obtained by sampling an edge and a common ambient seed,
   318	then applying the endpoint CL maps.  This is the inlined typed-CL construction
   319	of `def:pauli-question-distribution` (blueprint lines 285-329; paper
   320	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   321	-/
   322	noncomputable def pauliQuestionSupport (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   323	    Finset (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   324	  by
   325	    classical
   326	    exact
   327	      (Finset.univ.filter fun s : (PauliType × PauliType) × PauliSpace P =>
   328	          Sym2.mk s.1.1 s.1.2 ∈ pauliEdges).image (fun s =>
   329	        ((s.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   330	
   331	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   332	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   333	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   334	-/
   335	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   336	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   337	  by
   338	    classical
   339	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   340	    exact
   341	      Distribution.map
   342	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   343	        (fun s =>
   344	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   345	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))
   346	
   347	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   348	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   349	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   350	-/
   351	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   352	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   353	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   354	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   355	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   356	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   357	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   358	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   359	  deriving DecidableEq
   360	
   361	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   362	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   363	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   364	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   365	-/
   366	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   367	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   368	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   369	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   370	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   371	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   372	
   373	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   374	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   375	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   376	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   377	-/
   378	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   379	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   380	  toFun
   381	    | .value a => .inl a
   382	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   383	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   384	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   385	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   386	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   387	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   388	  invFun
   389	    | .inl a => .value a
   390	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   391	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   392	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   393	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   394	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   395	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

  1126	\paragraph{Decision procedure.}
  1127	The decision procedure for $\game^\pauli$ is presented in
  1128	Figure~\ref{fig:decider_pauli}.
  1129	Similarly to Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}, we provide a table that summarizes a
  1130	parsing scheme for the questions and answers, depending on the type of question.
  1131	The answers are bit strings that are interpreted as more structured objects such
  1132	as elements over $\F_q$, vectors, or polynomials, depending on the question.
  1133	In the ``low-degree check'', the decision procedure $\decider^\pauli$ calls the
  1134	classical low-degree decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ parametrized by the tuple
  1135	$\ldparams = (q,m,d,1)$ (defined in Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}) as a
  1136	subroutine.
  1137	
  1138	
  1139	\begin{figure}[H]
  1140	  \begin{gamespec}
  1141	    \vspace{9pt}
  1142	    \begin{center}

  1144	      \begin{tabularx}{.92\textwidth}{ l X l }
  1145	        \toprule
  1146	        Type & Question Content & Answer Format \\
  1147	        \midrule
  1148	        (\Point, $W$) & $y \in  \F_q^m$ & Element of $\F_q$  \\
  1149	        (\ALine, $W$) & $(u_W, s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$
  1150	        & Polynomial $f: \F_q \to \F_q$\\

  1152	        & Polynomial $f: \F_q \to \F_q$ \\
  1153	        \Pair & $(u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt) \in
  1154	        (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q^2 $ & $(\beta_\xpt,\beta_\zpt) \in \F_2^2$ \\
  1155	        (\Pair, $W$) & $(u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt) \in
  1156	        (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q^2 $ & Element of $\F_2$ \\
  1157	        $\Constraint_i$ & $(u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt) \in (\F_q^m)^2
  1158	        \times \F_q^2$ &
  1159	        $(\alpha_{v_1}, \alpha_{v_2}, \alpha_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$ \\
  1160	        $\Variable_j$ & $(u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt) \in
  1161	        (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q^2$ & Element of $\F_2$ \\
  1162	        (\Pauli, $W$) & $0$ & Element of $\F_q^{M}$ \\
  1163	        \bottomrule \multicolumn{3}{c}{Table: Question and answer format of the
  1164	          Pauli basis game.}
  1165	      \end{tabularx}
  1166	    \end{center}
  1167	    \vspace{9pt}
  1168	
  1169	    On input $(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice, \tvar_\bob, x_\bob, a_\alice, a_\bob)$,
  1170	    the decision procedure $\decider^\pauli$ performs the following checks for
  1171	    $w \in \AB$:
  1172	    \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,parsep=2pt]
  1173	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1174	      \label{item:same-type}
  1175	      If $\tvar_\alice = \tvar_\bob$, accept iff $a_\alice = a_\bob$.
  1176	
  1177	    \item (\textbf{Low-degree}).
  1178	      \label{item:low-degree}
  1179	      Let $\ldparams = (q,m,d,1)$. 
  1180	      \begin{enumerate}
  1181	      	\item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\ALine, W)$, accept if
  1182	      $\decider^\ld_{\ldparams}$ accepts $(\Point, x_w, \ALine, x_{\overline{w}}, a_w,
  1183	      a_{\overline{w}})$.
  1184	      	\item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\DLine, W)$, accept if
  1185	      $\decider^\ld_{\ldparams}$ accepts $(\Point, x_w, \DLine, x_{\overline{w}}, a_w,
  1186	      a_{\overline{w}})$.
  1187			\end{enumerate}
  1188	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1189	      \label{item:low-degree-consistency}
  1190	      If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\Pauli, W)$, accept if
  1191	      $g_{a_{\overline{w}}}(x_w) = a_w$, where $g_{a_{\overline{w}}}$ is
  1192	      the low-degree encoding of $a_{\overline{w}} \in \F_q^M$ defined in
  1193	      Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.
  1194	    \end{enumerate}
  1195	    In the remaining four cases, the decision procedure first computes the
  1196	    number
  1197	    \begin{equation}
  1198	      \label{eq:gamma-value}
  1199	      \gamma = \tr \bigl( (\ind_{m}(u_\xpt) \cdot r_\xpt) \cdot
  1200	      (\ind_{m}(u_\zpt) \cdot r_\zpt) \bigr)\;,
  1201	    \end{equation}
  1202	    where we recall the $\ind_{m}(\cdot)$ vector from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.
  1203	    \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,parsep=2pt]
  1204	      \setcounter{enumi}{3}
  1205	    \item (\textbf{Commutation check}).
  1206	      \label{item:commutation} If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} =
  1207	      \Pair$, accept if $a_w = \beta_W$ or $\gamma \neq 0$.
  1208	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1209	      \label{item:commutation-consistency} If $\tvar_w = (\Point,W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} =
  1210	      (\Pair,W)$, accept if $\tr (a_w r_W) = a_{\overline{w}}$ or $\gamma \neq 0$.
  1211	      
  1212	    \item (\textbf{Magic square check}).
  1213	      \label{item:magic-square} If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i,
  1214	      \tvar_{\overline{w}} = \Variable_j$, accept if $\gamma = 0$, or $a_w$
  1215	      satisfies constraint $\Constraint_i$ and $ \alpha_j = a_{\overline{w}}$.
  1216	
  1217	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1218	      \label{item:magic-square-consistency}

  1221	      a_{\overline{w}}$ or if $j = 5$, $W = Z$, and $\tr(a_w r_\zpt) =
  1222	      a_{\overline{w}}$.
  1223	    \end{enumerate}

    34	Besides the usual positivity assumptions, we bundle the paper-faithful witness

    51	/-- Any number presented as a prime power is automatically positive. -/
    52	theorem q_pos_of_primePower {q : ℕ}
    53	    (hqPrimePower : ∃ p n, Nat.Prime p ∧ 0 < n ∧ q = p ^ n) : 0 < q := by
    54	  rcases hqPrimePower with ⟨p, n, hp, hn, rfl⟩
    55	  exact Nat.pow_pos hp.pos

    57	/-- Prime numbers are prime powers of exponent `1`. -/
    58	theorem prime_primePower {q : ℕ} (hqPrime : Nat.Prime q) :
    59	    ∃ p n, Nat.Prime p ∧ 0 < n ∧ q = p ^ n := by
    60	  exact ⟨q, 1, hqPrime, by decide, by simp⟩
    61	
    62	/-- Build parameters from explicit prime-power data `q = p^n`. -/
    63	def ofPrimePower (m q d p n : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hn : 0 < n)

    65	  { m := m

/-- Any number presented as a prime power is automatically positive. -/
theorem q_pos_of_primePower {q : ℕ}
    (hqPrimePower : ∃ p n, Nat.Prime p ∧ 0 < n ∧ q = p ^ n) : 0 < q := by
  rcases hqPrimePower with ⟨p, n, hp, hn, rfl⟩
  exact Nat.pow_pos hp.pos

/-- Prime numbers are prime powers of exponent `1`. -/
theorem prime_primePower {q : ℕ} (hqPrime : Nat.Prime q) :
    ∃ p n, Nat.Prime p ∧ 0 < n ∧ q = p ^ n := by
  exact ⟨q, 1, hqPrime, by decide, by simp⟩

/-- Build parameters from explicit prime-power data `q = p^n`. -/
def ofPrimePower (m q d p n : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hn : 0 < n)

  { m := m
    q := q
    d := d
    hm := hm
    hq := q_pos_of_primePower ⟨p, n, hp, hn, hq⟩
    hqPrimePower := ⟨p, n, hp, hn, hq⟩ }

/-- Build parameters when `q` itself is prime. -/

  { m := m
    q := q
    d := d
    hm := hm
    hq := hqPrime.pos
    hqPrimePower := prime_primePower hqPrime }

theorem two_le_q (params : Parameters) : 2 ≤ params.q := by

    21	The low-degree test is used as a subroutine in the Pauli Basis test (see

    24	We describe the test as a nonlocal game in Section~\ref{sec:ld-game} and show
